column1: # --- 29150: audio driver. The DMA cache follows Nintendo's audiomgr sample (AMDMAState/AMDMABuffer); the sample's own names are not used, so these are behaviour names

column3: (rom, ram, size): one osPiStartDma on the audio queue D_8008F0B8 and waits; used by the sequence/bank loaders
called from Core_MainThread: alHeapInit 0x68000 at D_80332DB0, allocates the command lists and output buffers, sets the 22050 Hz synth config (dmaproc Audio_DmaNew) and calls alInit
the ALDMAproc callback returned by Audio_DmaNew: reuses a cached 0x500-byte ROM buffer that covers addr+len, otherwise takes a free one, starts osPiStartDma, returns the physical address
the synth config's dmaproc: on first call links 32 buffers of 0x500 bytes into the free list; returns Audio_DmaCallback
moves DMA buffers unused for more than 2 audio frames back to the free list, resets the per-frame DMA count and increments the frame counter D_80055938; called each frame by the audio thread

thread started by Audio_StartThread: nnScAddClient, then on each NN_SC_RETRACE_MSG (1) runs Audio_UpdateFrame, builds an alAudioFrame task and sends it to nnScGetAudioMQ; on NN_SC_PRE_NMI_MSG (3) fades both sequence players to 0 and stops output
reads the ALSeqFile header (4 bytes) from ROM, then reallocates and reads the full seqArray (seqCount * 8 + 4)
osCreateThread(D_8008CEC0, id 5, Audio_ThreadMain, arg, pri 0x32) and osStartThread; called from Core_MainThread
allocates two 0x8000 sequence buffers, creates two ALCSPlayers (D_8008F7A8[0..1]), loads the seq file header and the bank file, sets bank 0 on both players
(slot, seqNo): DMAs seqArray[seqNo] into the slot's buffer and stores seqNo
(slot): if the slot's player is stopped, alCSeqNew on its buffer, alCSPSetSeq, alSeqpPlay, FX mix 0x18 on all 16 channels, returns 1; else 0
(slot): alSeqpStop on the slot's player
(slot): returns alSeqpGetState of the slot's player; Bgm_Update waits on it
loads the sound bank from ROM, alSndpNew (0x50 sounds), alSndpAllocate for every sound of instrument 0 into D_8008F4BC; called from Core_MainThread
(id): alSndpSetSound(D_8008F4BC[id]), and if it is stopped alSndpPlay with FX mix 0x10
(id): alSndpSetSound(D_8008F4BC[id]) and alSndpStop
(id): alSndpSetSound then alSndpGetState (the C discards the value but it is left in v0); uncalled

called by Audio_ThreadMain each retrace: counts down the 5 sound-script channels and steps their scripts (Sfx_StepScript), retries a pending sequence request, steps sequence fade-out/in, then Sfx_ProcessQueue
(id): sets the script pointer D_8008F75C to D_80055A24[id] for id 0..0x46, else entry 0

(req): 1 = play slot 1 at full volume; >= 0x50 = play seq req-0x50 in slot 0 fading in (step 0x100); else play seq req in slot 0 at full volume; keeps the request pending in D_800559BC while Audio_LoadSeqsOrStop must stop players first
(id): Sfx_Enqueue with volume factor 0 (script volume) and pan 0x40 into the 8-entry ring D_8005594C/6C/8C; uncalled
(id, volume factor, pan): writes the request to the 8-entry ring D_8005594C/D_8005596C/D_8005598C at D_800559B0; Sfx_Play and the overlays call it

takes one request from the ring: scripts whose first word is nonzero go to channel 4 (replacing its sound), others to channel (index & 3), stopping duplicates; Audio_PlaySound, then the first Sfx_StepScript

runs one step of the current channel's script: 0xFFFF stops the sound, 0xFFFD/0xFFFE mark/jump back for loops, then duration, pitch (D_8004F780), volume (scaled by the request factor) and pan; saves the script pointers per channel
lowers the active player's volume D_800559C4[D_800559B8] by D_800559CC; below 0 stops that player and ends the fade
raises the active player's volume by D_800559D0 up to the limit D_800559B4, then ends the fade
(seqNo): if the active player is stopped, Audio_LoadSeq(0, seqNo) and Audio_LoadSeq(1, 1), returns 0; else stops both players and returns 1
(frames): unless a fade runs (returns 1), sets the fade-out step D_800559CC = 0x8000 / frames and returns 0; called by Player_StateTalk, the overlays and others
stops the sound of each of the 5 script channels and clears their timers and ids; called by the Core_Run* loops
stops channel 4's sound (D_800559D4[4]) and clears its timer; MapObj_DrawNearby calls it when the map's distance sound ends
(vol 0..255): unless a fade runs (returns 1), sets the limit D_800559B4 = vol * 128 + 0x7F on both sequence players and returns 0

column1: # --- 2B0F0: BGM and sound requests (Quest 64 US twin file: bgm.c)

column3: called from Core_MainThread: clears the BGM flags/delay, current and next BGM = -1, sound volume D_8008FAF4 = 0xFF, the 16 delayed-sound slots

per frame from the Core_Run* loops: after the change delay stops the current sequence (Audio_StopSeq), when stopped loads and plays the next one (Audio_LoadSeq/Audio_PlaySeq, Bgm_ApplyVolumeOption); fires delayed sounds via Sfx_Enqueue
(bgm): if different from the current D_8008FAF0, stores it as next and sets the change flag; Quest 64 twin named UpdateBGM in Rainchus dump.toml (kind changed)
(bgm, delay): as Bgm_Play, with the change delay D_8008FAF6 in frames
(map, submap, delay): looks up D_80055B40 (map, submap or -1 for any) and requests its BGM like Bgm_PlayDelayed; Core_RunGameplayLoop, Player_StateBattleWon
(delay, id, vol): volume = per-sound D_80055CF8[id] * vol * D_8008FAF4 >> 16; delay 0 calls Sfx_Enqueue(id, volume, 0x40), else stores it in a free delayed slot; called from 66 places with sound ids
(id, vol): same volume formula as Sfx_Play, Sfx_Enqueue only when the result is nonzero; MapObj_DrawNearby plays the map's distance sound with it
Audio_SetSeqVolume(D_80055CF0[D_80060CB0]): D_80060CB0 is the 0..4 option row on Menu_DrawOptionsPage (saved by 30600)
